name: ChatGPT
good_for: Great for chatting, writing, homework help, planning trips, and turning word descriptions into pictures.
watch_out: The free plan is limited and can show ads; the cheapest paid plan (Go) costs $8 a month.

name: Claude
good_for: Great for writing help, summarizing long documents, answering coding questions, and thinking ideas through carefully.
watch_out: The free plan runs out of messages fast on busy days; the Pro plan costs $20 a month when billed monthly.

name: Gemini
good_for: Great for quick answers, help inside Google apps like Gmail and Docs, and looking things up on the web.
watch_out: The free version has usage limits, and the paid AI Pro plan costs $19.99 a month.

name: Grok
good_for: Great for fun chats, quick questions, seeing what's happening on X right now, and making pictures from words.
watch_out: The free version only lets you ask so much each day, and the paid SuperGrok plan costs $30 a month; you need an X account to sign in.

name: Perplexity
good_for: Great for looking things up and getting answers that show exactly which websites the facts came from.
watch_out: The free plan only gives you a few deep searches each day; unlimited searches cost $20 a month.

name: Llama
good_for: Free, powerful AI you can download and run on your own computer or through Meta's own apps.
watch_out: You have to set it up yourself or use someone else's app to talk to it.

name: Mistral
good_for: A fast, free chatbot made in Europe that answers questions, searches the web, and even makes images.
watch_out: The free plan has daily limits, and the paid Vibe Pro plan costs $14.99 a month.

name: Qwen
good_for: A free AI chat assistant that is strong in many languages and can also generate images.
watch_out: Running its biggest versions on your own computer needs serious hardware.

name: Midjourney
good_for: Beautiful AI pictures and art that look great, made by typing a simple description.
watch_out: There is no free plan and your pictures are public unless you pay more.

name: Stable Diffusion
good_for: Free AI picture-making that runs on your own computer with no subscription and no picture limits.
watch_out: You have to install it yourself and your computer needs a good graphics card.

name: Flux
good_for: It makes very detailed pictures from a short written description, like posters, art, or product mockups.
watch_out: Setting it up on your own computer takes some technical steps and a strong graphics card.

name: ElevenLabs
good_for: It turns your written words into natural-sounding spoken audio, great for videos, podcasts, or audiobooks.
watch_out: The free plan is small, so you will hit the monthly limit quickly if you make lots of audio.

name: Suno
good_for: It turns a few words about a style or theme into a full song with music and singing.
watch_out: Songs made on the free plan cannot be used for business or sold.

name: Runway
good_for: It turns your words or photos into short video clips for ads, social posts, or creative projects.
watch_out: You spend credits for each second of video, so longer videos use them up fast.

name: Cursor
good_for: It is an app where an AI assistant helps you write, fix, and explain code right in your editor.
watch_out: The free plan only includes a small number of AI requests each month.

good_for: It turns spoken audio into written text, great for transcribing meetings, lectures, or video subtitles. It understands dozens of languages.
name: Whisper
watch_out: You have to install it yourself with some command-line steps, and it needs a decent computer to run well.

good_for: It turns your written descriptions into short, realistic-looking video clips, even with matching sound.
name: Sora
watch_out: Free users only get a limited number of clips each day, and longer videos without watermarks need a paid plan.

good_for: Google's top video maker; it turns words or photos into sharp, cinematic video clips, even with matching sound.
name: Veo
watch_out: The cheapest official way in is the Google AI Pro plan at $20 a month; you pay per second of video, so costs add up fast.

good_for: It turns your words or photos into short, fun video clips with playful effects like melting or exploding objects.
name: Pika
watch_out: The free plan gives you only a few short clips a month, and free clips carry a watermark.

good_for: It turns words or photos into smooth, realistic-looking video clips, and you get free credits every day.
name: Kling
watch_out: The free daily credits only cover short clips, and longer or watermark-free videos need a paid plan.

good_for: It turns a short description into a full song with music, singing, and lyrics that you can tweak and extend.
name: Udio
watch_out: Songs made on the free plan are public and cannot be used for business.

good_for: An AI helper that does multi-step jobs for you on its own, like researching a topic and building a report or a website.
name: Manus
watch_out: It spends credits on every task, so long jobs can burn through your plan quickly; always double-check its work.

good_for: An AI software engineer that can plan, write, and test code for whole projects on its own in the cloud.
name: Devin
watch_out: It charges for the computer time it uses, so a big job can cost more than the $20 starting price.

good_for: It suggests code as you type right inside your editor, and it can explain code and help fix bugs.
name: GitHub Copilot
watch_out: The free plan only includes a limited number of completions and chats each month.

good_for: An AI coding helper that works in your terminal; it can read your whole project, make changes, and run tests.
name: Claude Code
watch_out: There is no free access, and usage limits mean heavy coding days can hit the cap.

good_for: You describe an app in plain words and its AI agent builds it and puts it on the web, all in your browser.
name: Replit
watch_out: The free plan only includes small daily AI credits, and extra AI usage costs more.

good_for: A smarter way to Google: it gives full AI answers with links, and you can ask follow-up questions.
name: Google AI Mode
watch_out: It is built into Google Search, so you need to be signed in to a Google account to use it.

good_for: A private search engine that answers questions with AI and shows exactly which websites the facts came from.
name: You.com
watch_out: The free version limits how many AI searches you can do each day.

good_for: A free app that downloads AI models like Llama and DeepSeek and runs them on your own computer, with no internet needed after setup.
name: Ollama
watch_out: You type commands to use it, the bigger models need lots of computer memory, and the new paid Ollama Pro plan costs $20 a month.

good_for: A free AI chat assistant that is strong at math, coding, and careful step-by-step thinking.
name: DeepSeek
watch_out: Your chats are stored on servers in China, so do not share private details with it.

good_for: Great for making logos, posters, and designs that include words — it spells text inside pictures better than most other tools.
name: Ideogram
watch_out: Pictures you make on the free plan are public for everyone to see, and you can't keep them private without paying; paid plans start at $15 a month.

good_for: Great for game art, character designs, and keeping the same art style across many pictures.
name: Leonardo AI
watch_out: It uses a credit system instead of a simple price, so free users only get 150 credits a day, and keeping pictures private needs a paid plan.

good_for: Great for business-ready pictures that are safe to use commercially, since it is trained on licensed content.
name: Adobe Firefly
watch_out: The free plan only gives 25 credits a month, and unused credits do not roll over to the next month.

good_for: Great for making social media posts, flyers, and presentations with AI help, right inside an easy drag-and-drop design tool.
name: Canva AI (Magic Studio)
watch_out: The free plan only gives a small number of AI uses each month, and Canva prices change by country, so check the pricing page for your own price.

good_for: Turns your written text into a video with a realistic AI talking person, so you can make studio-quality videos without a camera, actors, or editing skills.
name: HeyGen
watch_out: You pay with credits and each video costs credits, so making lots of videos can get expensive; the free plan also only gives 3 videos a month and adds a watermark.

good_for: It turns a written description or a photo into a realistic short video clip, like making a still photo move or describing a scene and watching it come to life.
name: Luma Dream Machine
watch_out: Clips are short (about 5 to 10 seconds each), and the paid Plus plan costs $30 a month, so you likely need to pay before you can create anything.

good_for: It turns your words or photos into short AI videos in just a few clicks.
name: Hailuo AI
watch_out: The free version puts a watermark on your videos, and clips are short — only about 6 to 10 seconds each.

good_for: Murf is best at turning typed scripts into natural-sounding voiceovers for videos, podcasts, and presentations.
name: Murf AI
watch_out: On the free plan you cannot download your audio or use it in anything commercial — downloads and commercial rights need a paid plan.

good_for: It turns your written text into realistic spoken audio using over 600 voices in 142 languages and accents.
name: PlayAI (formerly PlayHT)
watch_out: It is priced by how much audio you make, so heavy use or voice cloning can get expensive fast.

good_for: You can ask it questions, write emails, and make pictures using plain words — no training needed, and the basic chat is free.
name: Microsoft Copilot
watch_out: The free version has usage limits; the paid Microsoft 365 Premium plan costs $19.99 a month. (Copilot Pro was discontinued.)

good_for: It's free and already lives inside WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger, so you can ask it things right where you already chat with people.
name: Meta AI
watch_out: Your conversations may be used to train Meta's AI models unless you opt out, so avoid sharing private details with it.

good_for: It connects your apps and does boring tasks for you — like saving email attachments to Google Drive — without writing any code, and an AI helper builds the workflows from a plain sentence.
name: Zapier AI
watch_out: The free plan covers only 100 tasks a month and caps workflows at two steps, so costs rise quickly as you automate more.

good_for: It lets you build powerful step-by-step automations across hundreds of apps, and the free Community edition runs on your own machine with no limits on executions.
name: n8n
watch_out: It's built for technical users, so the first setup can feel hard if you've never made a workflow before; the cloud plan costs $24 a month, or you can run it on your own computer for free.

good_for: It's a free, openly available AI model from Google (built with the same research as Gemini) that developers can download, customize, and build with.
name: Gemma
watch_out: Gemma is a raw model, not an app — you need technical tools to actually run it, so it's hard for non-technical people to use on its own.

good_for: It's a free desktop app that runs AI models right on your computer, so everything stays private and nothing you type is sent to the cloud.
name: LM Studio
watch_out: You need a fairly strong computer (at least 8GB of memory, 16GB recommended), and downloading a good model can take a while.

name: Character AI
good_for: Great for chatting and roleplaying with fun characters you pick or create yourself - story heroes, historical figures, and helpful personas.
watch_out: The free plan has daily limits, and the characters sometimes make things up; the paid plan costs $9.99 a month.

name: Poe
good_for: Great for trying many different AI models in one app - GPT, Claude, Llama, and more - and comparing their answers side by side.
watch_out: The free plan limits how much you can chat each day; the paid plan costs $4.99 a month.

name: DuckDuckGo AI Chat
good_for: Great for asking questions in private - it does not track you, and you can switch between models like GPT, Claude, and Llama.
watch_out: Chats are anonymous, so they are not saved when you leave the page; advanced AI models need the $9.99-a-month DuckDuckGo Plus plan.

name: OpenAI Codex
good_for: Great for programmers: it works inside your terminal, writes new features, fixes bugs, and runs your tests for you.
watch_out: It is a tool for people who code, not beginners; you need a paid ChatGPT plan to use it.

name: Windsurf
good_for: An AI code editor that understands your whole project and can change many files at once, with you watching each step.
watch_out: The free plan gives you a limited number of AI prompts each month; the Pro plan costs $20 a month. Windsurf is now part of Devin (Devin Desktop).

name: Lovable
good_for: Great for non-programmers: describe the app or website you want in plain words and it builds a working version for you.
watch_out: The free plan only gives you a few builds each day, and big projects use up credits fast; the Pro plan costs $25 a month.

name: Otter.ai
good_for: Joins your meetings and writes down what everyone says, so you get notes and summaries without typing a word.
watch_out: The free plan only covers a limited number of meeting minutes, and it needs access to join your calls; the Pro plan costs $16.99 a month.

name: Descript
good_for: Great for editing podcasts and videos by editing the written transcript - delete a sentence and it is gone from the recording, like editing a document.
watch_out: The free plan only includes about one hour of editing a month; paid plans start at $16 a month when billed yearly.

name: NotebookLM
good_for: Great for studying: upload your documents and ask it questions, or turn them into a podcast-style audio chat between two AI hosts.
watch_out: It only answers from the documents you upload, so weak sources mean weak answers.

name: Photoshop (generative fill)
good_for: Inside Photoshop, add or remove anything in a photo with a text prompt - the AI fills in the rest to match.
watch_out: You need a paid Photoshop or Creative Cloud plan, and it takes some practice to use well.

name: Remove.bg
good_for: Removes the background from any photo in seconds with one click - great for product shots and profile pictures.
watch_out: Free downloads are limited and smaller; full-quality images need credits or a plan.

name: CapCut AI
good_for: A free video editor from the maker of TikTok with AI captions, background removal, and text-to-speech built right in.
watch_out: Some features and cloud storage need the paid Pro plan; the paid Standard plan costs about $9.99 a month, and it is best for short videos, not full movies.

name: ChatGPT agent
good_for: Great for multi-step online chores: it browses the web, fills out forms, compares prices, and finishes tasks for you.
watch_out: It needs a paid ChatGPT plan, and you should check its work before it books or buys anything.

name: Perplexity Comet
good_for: A web browser with an AI assistant built in that can summarize pages, compare products, and do small tasks for you.
watch_out: It collects your browsing history to target ads, and the advanced agent features need a paid plan (Comet Plus costs $5 a month).

name: Kimi
good_for: A free chatbot that handles very long documents and searches the web, with open models you can also run yourself.
watch_out: It is made by a Chinese company, so think carefully about what personal details you share.

good_for: An AI assistant inside your code editor that suggests code and answers questions about your own codebase.
name: Tabnine
watch_out: The advertised price is the annual plan; no free individual tier is listed on the pricing page.

good_for: Amazon's AI coding helper that suggests code and answers questions inside your editor or the AWS console.
name: Amazon Q Developer
watch_out: The paid Pro subscription can start billing once you use certain AI features, not at sign-in, so it can surprise you with a charge.

good_for: Talk to an AI in your computer's terminal and it writes and edits your code files for you.
name: Aider
watch_out: The tool itself is free, but you still pay the AI provider (like Anthropic or OpenAI) for each use, so costs depend on how much you use it.

good_for: Describe the website or app you want in plain words and it builds it for you right in your browser.
name: Bolt.new
watch_out: Everything runs on tokens, so a big or complicated project can burn through your monthly allowance quickly.

good_for: Type a description and it creates images for you, with lots of ready-made style templates to start from.
name: Playground AI
watch_out: The free plan is slow and limited to a few images every few hours, and the premium models use monthly credits.

good_for: Chatting with free open-source AI models without paying anything.
name: HuggingChat
watch_out: Answer quality and uptime vary by model, and there is no paid tier if you ever want priority access.

good_for: Drafting marketing content and pulling live web data inside one chat window.
name: ChatSonic
watch_out: It is now folded into Writesonic's marketing platform, and the $16/month price is billed annually.

good_for: Talking through ideas or worries with a friendly, conversational AI.
name: Pi by Inflection
watch_out: It has no paid tier with extra features, and it cannot browse the live web or perform tasks for you.

good_for: Listening to articles, documents, and books read aloud in natural-sounding voices.
name: Speechify
watch_out: The free plan's voices sound robotic, and the natural-voice Premium plan costs $29/month.

good_for: Turning scripts into studio-quality voiceovers for videos and presentations.
name: WellSaid Labs
watch_out: You pay for downloaded minutes of finished audio, so long projects get expensive quickly.

good_for: Turn a text prompt into a finished video with stock footage and AI voiceover without editing anything yourself.
name: InVideo
watch_out: Paid plans run on credits that do not roll over, and costs are hard to predict because every AI model burns credits at a different rate.

good_for: Turn a long video or podcast into short vertical clips with captions for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.
name: Opus Clip
watch_out: You pay per minute of video you upload, not per clip you get, so long source videos burn through the plan fast.

good_for: Turn a blog post, script, or long recording into a captioned video with stock footage matched to your words.
name: Pictory
watch_out: Exports top out at 1080p, there is no ongoing free plan (14-day trial only), and unused video minutes do not roll over.

good_for: Type a script and get a video of a lifelike AI presenter saying it, in over 160 languages.
name: Synthesia
watch_out: The $29 Starter plan covers only about 120 minutes of finished video for the whole year, so steady publishing means a bigger plan.

good_for: Type a script and get a training-style video narrated by an AI avatar, with quizzes and course exports.
name: Colossyan
watch_out: The paid plan starts at $59/month, one of the priciest entries here, and it is built for training videos rather than creative content.

good_for: Create original songs in over 250 styles in seconds, even with no music training.
name: AIVA
watch_out: The free and Standard plans keep copyright with AIVA and limit commercial use; only the Pro plan transfers full ownership to you.

good_for: Generate royalty-free background music from a text prompt for videos, podcasts, and apps.
name: Mubert
watch_out: The free plan adds an audible watermark and requires attribution, and tracks can't be released on Spotify or registered with Content ID.

good_for: Ask a research question and get structured evidence tables pulled from over 138 million academic papers.
name: Elicit
watch_out: Elicit works on usage limits, so heavy extraction runs can burn through your monthly allowance faster than expected.

good_for: Check whether scientific papers are supported or contradicted by later research, with AI-written summaries.
name: Scite
watch_out: The free plan only covers the basic research connector, not the full platform; real literature-review work starts at the paid Basic plan.

good_for: Build an AI voice assistant that answers and makes real phone calls for your business.
name: Vapi
watch_out: The headline per-minute fee only covers Vapi's own charge — the AI model, voice, and phone line each add separate costs on top.

good_for: An AI teammate that handles your email, calendar, meetings, and routine office work when you tell it what to do.
name: Lindy
watch_out: Everything runs on credits, so heavy or complex tasks can burn through your monthly allowance faster than the plan price suggests.

good_for: Build chatbots and conversational forms for your website by dragging and dropping blocks, no coding needed.
name: Typebot
watch_out: Chat limits count every new conversation, so a busy site can burn through the free 200 chats a month quickly.

good_for: Build an AI chatbot or support agent for your website, WhatsApp, or Slack that answers questions and can do real tasks.
name: Botpress
watch_out: Plan prices don't include AI usage and extra conversation packs, which are billed on top and can add up fast.

good_for: Turns a written script into a spoken voiceover or narrated video in hundreds of voices and languages.
name: Narakeet
watch_out: Free accounts cannot be used for commercial projects, and every full build (including re-doing one) eats your paid minutes.

good_for: Edits videos in a web browser with AI tools for subtitles, voiceovers, resizing, and background removal.
name: Kapwing
watch_out: Free exports carry a Kapwing watermark and are limited to short 720p clips, and the AI features run on a limited monthly credit allowance.

good_for: Automatically cuts silences, adds subtitles and background music, and turns long videos into short clips.
name: Wisecut
watch_out: The free plan only exports at 360p, and paid plans run on a monthly credit balance that long videos can burn through quickly.

good_for: Builds no-code AI agents that can do multi-step work across apps, like sales research or lead follow-up.
name: Relevance AI
watch_out: Everything is metered in Actions and credits, so real usage costs can climb past the base plan, and the builder still takes genuine setup effort.

name: Copy.ai
good_for: Writing marketing copy, emails, and social posts fast with AI that follows your brand voice.
watch_out: The $24/month Chat plan is billed once a year ($288 up front); month to month costs $29.

name: Soundful
good_for: Generating royalty-free background music for videos, streams, and social posts.
watch_out: The $9.99/month Plus plan is billed monthly; the cheaper $4.99 rate needs a full year paid upfront, and downloads reset each month.

name: Getimg.ai
good_for: Generating and editing AI images for art, thumbnails, and design mockups.
watch_out: The $8/month Entry plan is billed yearly ($96 upfront), plan credits do not roll over, and API access costs extra.

name: Augment Code
good_for: Getting AI help writing and understanding code right inside your code editor.
watch_out: The $20/month plan is a usage allowance across their AI models, so heavy coding sessions can burn through it.

name: Gumloop
good_for: Building no-code AI automations that scrape sites, process data, and run on a schedule.
watch_out: Pro starts at $37/month and usage is credit-based, so large workflows can cost more than the base price.

name: Kagi
good_for: Ad-free web search with better results and no tracking.
watch_out: The $5/month Starter plan limits how many searches you get; heavy searching needs a pricier plan.

name: Kits AI
good_for: Training AI voices to sing or speak for your music tracks.
watch_out: The cheapest paid plan is Starter at $10 a month, and it limits how many custom voices you can train.

name: Listnr
good_for: Turning text into natural voiceovers for videos and podcasts.
watch_out: The $19/month plan caps you at 20,000 credits, which is roughly 2 hours of audio a month.

name: LTX Studio
good_for: Directing AI-generated video scenes with real camera-style controls.
watch_out: The $12/month price needs yearly billing and is currently shown as a limited-time offer, and the plan caps you at 8,000 credits a month.

name: Dzine.ai
good_for: Editing photos and generating design images with simple text prompts.
watch_out: The $8.99/month plan is credit-based, and extra top-up credits cost more on top.

name: Cartesia
good_for: Adding ultra-fast, natural AI voices to apps and products.
watch_out: The $5/month Pro plan bundles 100K credits a month; go over the included credits and you pay for more.

name: Fireflies.ai
good_for: Auto-transcribing meetings and getting AI summaries without taking notes.
watch_out: The $10/month price needs yearly billing, and the plan covers a set number of transcription minutes per month.

name: Krisp
good_for: Removing background noise from your calls and meetings.
watch_out: The $8/month price needs yearly billing ($16 month-to-month), and it is priced per user.

name: Reclaim.ai
good_for: Auto-scheduling your workday, habits, and meetings around your priorities.
watch_out: The $10 Starter price needs yearly billing and is per seat; month to month it is $12 each, so costs add up as your team grows.

name: Jasper
good_for: Writing on-brand marketing content with an AI trained on your style.
watch_out: The $59/month Pro price needs yearly billing; month-to-month is $69, and it is built for teams rather than casual use.

name: Rytr
good_for: Writing short marketing copy and emails on a tight budget.
watch_out: The $7.50 Unlimited plan needs yearly billing, so you pay about $90 up front rather than month to month.

name: Fathom
good_for: Recording video calls with free transcripts and AI summaries.
watch_out: The cheapest plan one person can buy is Premium at $16 a month on yearly billing ($20 month to month); the Team price advertised as $15 needs at least 2 users.

good_for: It turns a genre, mood, and length you pick into an original royalty-free track - the AI is trained only on music their own producers write and record, and every download comes with a worldwide, perpetual license.
name: Soundraw
watch_out: The cheapest Creator plan only downloads MP3s. WAV files and separate instrument stems need the Artist Pro plan - Artist Starter is MP3-only too.

good_for: It splits any song into vocals, drums, bass, and other stems in seconds, and cleans up noisy recordings - with desktop, phone, and DAW apps.
name: LALAL.AI
watch_out: Paid plans give unlimited relaxed-queue minutes but only a fixed monthly amount of fast-queue minutes (90 on Lite, 250 on Pro); the VST plugin and local desktop processing are Pro-only.

good_for: Chat with an AI co-producer to make full songs with vocals, then publish and share them - the free plan tops up credits daily with no credit card required.
name: Flow Music
watch_out: The $6 price needs yearly billing; the page defaults to the yearly toggle, so month-to-month costs more. The free plan's daily credit top-ups are small.

good_for: Meta's open music-generation model you can download and run on your own computer - describe a style and it composes a matching track.
name: MusicGen
watch_out: It is a raw model, not an app - running it locally takes some coding, and the CC-BY-NC license on the weights rules out commercial use.

good_for: A search engine built for AI apps and agents - it returns clean webpage text and highlights instead of ad-filled results pages.
name: Exa
watch_out: This is a developer API, not a search box - you write code to call it. You can start free: $20 of credits at sign-up plus $10 monthly, no card required.

good_for: An open-source AI coding assistant that runs on your own servers or computer - code completion, in-editor chat, and answers grounded in your codebase, all kept private.
name: Tabby
watch_out: The paid Team plan is priced per person ($19 a seat), and the free Community plan covers up to 5 users.

good_for: A free desktop app that downloads open AI models and chats with them entirely on your computer - nothing you type ever leaves your machine.
name: GPT4All
watch_out: It is built for developers, teams, and AI power users rather than total beginners - expect to pick and configure your own models.

good_for: A free, open-source desktop app that runs AI chat models on your computer - like ChatGPT, but your conversations stay private on your machine.
name: Jan
watch_out: Bigger models are large downloads, and the online-model options connect to your own accounts with those providers.

good_for: A free, open-source desktop app that turns your own documents into a private AI assistant - chat with your files and get meeting summaries, all on your device with no accounts or API keys.
name: AnythingLLM
price_from: Free to run yourself (team cloud from $50/month)
watch_out: The desktop app that runs on your own computer is free. Their hosted team version starts at $50 a month.

good_for: The open standard for serious AI image and video work - connect models and processing steps as visible nodes on a canvas for total control over every step.
name: ComfyUI
price_from: Free to run yourself (cloud from $16/month billed annually)
watch_out: Free on your own computer, but their hosted Comfy Cloud starts at $16 a month on yearly billing. The node-canvas workflow takes real learning - start from a community template.

good_for: The easiest way to run Stable Diffusion on a Mac - text-to-image, generative fill, upscaling, and video tools in one free app that works fully offline.
name: DiffusionBee
watch_out: Mac only, and Apple silicon is recommended - Intel Macs work but generate images much more slowly.

name: Vocal Remover
price_from: Free (up to 10 minutes of audio a day); membership US$12.95/month or US$99/year
good_for: Splitting a song into karaoke (no vocals) and acapella (isolated vocals) tracks; also key, BPM, pitch and cutter tools
watch_out: The newer, better version is for paying members; free use is capped at 10 minutes of audio a day and 8-minute files

name: Tavily
price_from: Free (Researcher plan); paid from $0.008/credit (Pay As You Go) or $30/month (Project)
good_for: Search API built for AI agents — fast results with source citations
watch_out: API only, no consumer search page; usage-based pricing needs monitoring

name: goose
good_for: A free, open-source AI assistant on your own computer (desktop app or command line) that does tasks for you - coding, research, writing and automation
watch_out: You connect your own AI model (an API key or an existing Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini subscription), and that model's costs are separate

name: Qodo
good_for: Agentic AI code review on pull requests — rules system, pre-PR checks, analytics
watch_out: $30/month buys 2,500 credits (about 18 reviews a month); about 36 reviews costs $60/month. 14-day free trial; free only for open-source projects

name: Pieces
price_from: $18.99 per user/month (Pro, billed monthly; 25% off billed yearly)
good_for: An app that quietly remembers what you work on across your computer so you can ask AI about it later - recaps, meeting prep, finding past work
watch_out: No free plan (the 7-day trial needs a card); it captures what is on your screen every 2 seconds by default, so check its privacy settings

name: Replicate
price_from: Pay as you go per model - e.g. $0.025 per image (flux-dev), $0.04 per image (flux-1.1-pro)
good_for: Trying thousands of AI models (images, video, speech, music, chat) from one account, in a browser playground or through code
watch_out: Built for developers and billed per use - every run costs money, with no flat monthly plan

name: Mureka
good_for: Generating original songs, background music, soundscapes and AI music videos from text prompts
watch_out: Free plan: 4 songs a day on the free model; Pro: up to 500 songs a month with MP3 downloads only (WAV and stems need Premier, $30/month)

name: Loudly
good_for: AI text-to-music with commercial licensing and distribution to Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube Music
watch_out: Personal: 2,500 credits/month; free plan is non-commercial with 1 download per day

name: Boomy
price_from: $14.99/month (Creator list price; the page currently shows a 33% discount)
good_for: Making and releasing original AI songs with full commercial rights, even with no music experience
watch_out: Free plan: 25 song saves, no downloads, no commercial use; Creator includes 25 WAV downloads per month

name: Stable Audio
good_for: Generating royalty-free tracks with the Stable Audio web app and DAW plugin
watch_out: Solo: 660 credits/month; credits reset monthly and do not roll over

name: iAsk
good_for: AI search with an AI writer, instant summarizer and document analysis
watch_out: Pro: 300 daily Pro searches; free tier has limited ads and uses the non-Pro model

name: Recraft
good_for: Generating and editing images with multiple AI models (Flux, GPT Image, Nano Banana); video generation on Pro
watch_out: Basic: 1,000 credits/month; free-plan images are public with no commercial use

name: v0
good_for: Generating complete web apps and UIs from text prompts, deployed to Vercel
watch_out: Plus is priced per user; free plan limited to 7 messages per day

name: Warp
good_for: AI-assisted coding in a modern terminal with Warp Agent
watch_out: Build: 1,500 credits ($20 of agent usage at API rates); extra usage is pay-as-you-go

name: Zed
good_for: A fast code editor with AI edit predictions and token-based AI features
watch_out: Pro includes $5 of tokens; usage beyond that bills at API list price +10%

good_for: Running a private Perplexity-style AI answering engine entirely on your own hardware, with cited answers and local LLMs.
name: Vane
watch_out: You install and run it yourself (the guide recommends Docker), then connect an AI model: Ollama on your own computer, or a paid key from a provider like OpenAI, Claude or Groq.

good_for: Ad-free conversational answers and visual search results with a privacy-first, no-tracking positioning.
name: Andi
price_from: Free (a separate Search API for developers is paid per query)
watch_out: AI answers can contain mistakes (its terms say so), so check the sources it shows. Only the search site is free; the developer Search API is paid.

good_for: Free AI search across scientific papers, with one-line summaries of each paper and links to the papers it cites.
name: Semantic Scholar
watch_out: Academic literature only — it is not a general web search engine.

good_for: Evidence-backed answers and AI summaries drawn directly from peer-reviewed papers, with unlimited Pro messages.
name: Consensus
watch_out: $20/month is the monthly price ($12/month if you pay for a year). Pro includes 15 Deep reviews a month; the Free plan gets 10 Pro messages and up to 3 Deep reviews a month.

good_for: Self-hosted autonomous deep-research agents that aggregate 20+ web sources into cited reports on your own machine.
name: GPT Researcher
watch_out: You must bring your own paid AI and search accounts (for example OpenAI and Tavily), and each deep research run takes about 5 minutes.

good_for: AI singing voices from your melody and lyrics, voice cloning, and AI instruments that work alongside music-making software.
name: ACE Studio
watch_out: Generative kits, stem splitter, and video tools are metered from a 2,500 credits/month pool on the Artist plan.

good_for: Natural-sounding text-to-speech and voice cloning from as little as 10 seconds of audio, in 30+ languages; the company also shares downloadable models you can run yourself.
name: Fish Audio
watch_out: Free Tier is for personal use only; monetizing content requires a paid plan, and unused credits do not roll over.

good_for: AI voices that react to your tone: spoken back-and-forth chat, text-to-speech and voice cloning, mainly for people building apps.
name: Hume AI
watch_out: Starter includes about 30 minutes of text-to-speech and 40 minutes of AI voice chat a month; the price table shows no pay-for-more rate on Starter, so heavier use means upgrading.

good_for: Production phone and web voice agents with SIP telephony, no-code builder, and 20 free concurrent calls.
name: Retell AI
watch_out: Made for businesses building phone-answering bots. The real cost per minute depends on the parts you pick: Retell's voice engine is $0.055/minute, plus the AI model and the voice (Retell's own voices add $0.015/minute).

good_for: Free, expressive text-to-speech you can run yourself, with emotion tags (like laughing or sighing) and voice cloning from a short sample.
name: Orpheus TTS
watch_out: There is no app to click: you install it with Python commands and run it as code. The main models are English; other languages are only a research preview.

good_for: Automated transcription in 54+ languages with in-browser editing, translation, and subtitle exports.
name: Sonix
watch_out: Core includes 1 user and 5 hrs/month of transcription; extra seats are +$25/month each.

good_for: AI image upscaling on desktop (Linux, macOS, Windows); cloud plans add AI image generation.
name: Upscayl
price_from: Free to run yourself (Pro cloud from $9.99/month)
watch_out: The free desktop app needs a graphics card that supports Vulkan; many built-in (integrated) laptop graphics chips do not work.

good_for: Running open Stable Diffusion checkpoints locally: txt2img, img2img, inpainting, LoRAs, extensions.
name: AUTOMATIC1111 Stable Diffusion WebUI
watch_out: You must install Python and git first; the guide says a graphics card with 4GB+ of memory is needed.

good_for: Simple, offline text-to-image on your own computer: type a description, fix parts of a picture, or add a style.
name: Fooocus
watch_out: Needs 4GB+ Nvidia VRAM, 8GB RAM, 40GB free disk; project is in limited long-term support (bug fixes only).

good_for: AI product photography: background removal/replacement, AI backgrounds, marketing assets.
name: Photoroom
watch_out: Pro includes 8,000 AI credits and 1,000 exports a month; the Video Generator and 4K output are not included in Pro.

good_for: Breeding and remixing character portraits/art with gene sliders (Splicer, Collage, Composer).
name: Artbreeder
watch_out: Monthly Starter gives 100 credits a month (the page says about 1,000 images), and unused credits reset each billing period instead of rolling over.

good_for: AI photo enhancement: denoise, sharpen, upscale, face recovery.
name: Topaz Photo
watch_out: Commercial use limited to orgs under $1M USD annual revenue.

name: Ecrett Music
good_for: Making simple background music for videos, games and podcasts: pick a scene, mood and style, and its AI makes a new tune you can use without paying extra each time
watch_out: The free plan only downloads preview music, which you may not publish or use to make money. To use tracks in your videos you need Individual ($7.99/month). The music is meant to go inside videos, games or podcasts, not to be sold or shared as songs on their own

name: Fadr
good_for: Using AI to pull a song apart into separate tracks (vocals, drums, bass, melody) and remix it, even with no music experience
watch_out: The free plan splits songs into the main parts and gives MP3 downloads only. Finer splits (like single drums), higher-quality WAV files and the add-ons for music software need Fadr Plus

name: Onyx
price_from: Free to run yourself (Onyx cloud $20 per user/month, billed annually)
good_for: AI chat and search across a team's work files and apps (like Slack, Google Drive and Confluence), in Onyx's cloud or installed on your own server
watch_out: Made for teams at work. The $20 per person price is only offered with yearly billing. The free version means installing it yourself on a computer or server you manage, which takes technical skill

name: Cline
price_from: Free app (you pay for the AI as you use it, or ClinePass $9.99/month)
good_for: An AI helper that plans, writes and changes code for you, inside the VS Code code editor, in a command window, or in a new desktop app (still in testing)
watch_out: The app is free, but the AI it uses is not: you buy AI credits as you go, connect your own paid account from a company like OpenAI or Anthropic, or subscribe to ClinePass ($9.99/month). Made for people who write code

name: OpenHands
price_from: Free (you pay for the AI at cost or use your own key; Enterprise plan for companies is custom-priced)
good_for: Open-source AI helpers that write and fix software for you, either installed free on your own computer or used on the OpenHands website
watch_out: Built for software developers. The free website plan allows 1 user and 10 conversations a day. Either way you pay for the AI itself, at cost through OpenHands or with your own paid account from an AI company

name: Komo
good_for: Asking questions and getting AI answers with links to the sources; paid plans add deep research and top AI models
watch_out: The free plan gives 25 credits a day and only Komo's fast and budget AI models. Deep research, people search and top models like GPT, Claude and Gemini need Komo Pro ($20/month for 2,000 credits)

name: Kilo Code
price_from: Free (AI model usage is billed separately; Teams plan $15/user/month)
good_for: An AI coding helper you add to VS Code or JetBrains, or run in the terminal. It can use free models, models on your own computer, or your own keys from other AI companies.
watch_out: The tool itself is free, but the AI models it talks to cost money unless you pick the free or local ones.

name: OpenCode
price_from: Free (free models included; OpenCode Go from $10/month)
good_for: An open source AI coding helper for the terminal, a desktop app or your code editor. Connect almost any AI model, including ones on your own computer.
watch_out: Some of the free models are listed as available for a limited time. The $10/month Go plan has request limits every 5 hours and every month, set per model.

name: Kiro
good_for: A downloadable AI coding editor and command-line tool from Amazon that works as a coding agent on your projects.
watch_out: The free plan gives 50 credits and only some AI models, with rate limits. On the paid plans, extra credits cost $0.04 each.

name: JetBrains AI
price_from: Free (3 AI Credits per 30 days); AI Pro $10/month
good_for: AI chat, code suggestions and a coding helper built into JetBrains code editors such as IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm.
watch_out: You need a JetBrains code editor installed to use it. The free plan has only 3 AI Credits per 30 days, and AI Pro has 10.

name: Zencoder
price_from: $45/user/month (Pro plan, billed monthly; 7-day Pro trial, no free plan)
good_for: An AI coding helper that plugs into popular code editors and works with models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, or your own keys.
watch_out: There is no free plan, only a 7-day trial. Pro includes 30,000 credits a month, and extra credits are sold as top-ups.

name: Hedra
good_for: Makes AI video, images and talking avatars from a prompt, in a web studio with an AI assistant.
watch_out: There is no free plan in the price table, and making videos uses paid credits. Basic gives 2,000 credits a month with slower generations; faster generation starts at $50/month on the Pro plan.

name: VEED
good_for: A web video editor with AI subtitles, AI voices, avatars and video generation, so you can edit and polish clips in one place.
watch_out: The Creator plan includes 500 credits a month for the AI tools. Pro costs $45/month for 2,500 credits. Paying yearly is cheaper.

name: Fliki
good_for: Turns a script, blog post or slides into a video with a realistic AI voice, stock footage and music.
watch_out: The free plan makes 720p videos with a Fliki watermark and gives only 3 credits a month. Standard gives 180 credits a month.

name: Lumen5
good_for: Turns a blog post, link or script into a short social video with AI help. Built mainly for business use.
watch_out: The free plan allows 5 videos a month, up to 2 minutes each, with a Lumen5 branded outro. The Basic plan removes the branding.

name: Scira
good_for: An AI search engine that answers with sources from the web, Reddit, X, YouTube and academic papers. The code is open source.
watch_out: The free plan allows only 3 searches a day. Pro has unlimited searches, but some top models have monthly or weekly caps.

name: Paperguide
price_from: Free (2,000 AI credits a month); Plus $19/month
good_for: An AI research helper that finds papers, answers questions about them with citations and helps write literature reviews.
watch_out: The free plan gives 2,000 AI credits a month, with limited AI searches and a limited reference manager. Plus gives 12,500 credits.

name: ACE-Step
price_from: Free to download and run yourself
good_for: An open music model that makes full songs from a text description and lyrics on your own computer, with a simple web screen to use it.
watch_out: Setup is technical: you install it with Python, or use the ready-made download for Windows or Mac. It runs best with a strong graphics card and can be slow without one.

name: Ultimate Vocal Remover
good_for: A free desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux that splits a song into vocals and instruments using AI models, for karaoke tracks and remixing.
watch_out: Splitting runs on your own computer, so it can be slow without a good graphics card. You download the AI models you want to use.

name: Spleeter
good_for: A free tool from Deezer that splits a song into 2, 4 or 5 parts such as vocals, drums and bass, using ready-trained AI models.
watch_out: It is a Python command-line tool with no app window, so it suits people comfortable installing software.

name: YuE2
good_for: An open music model that turns your lyrics and a style description into a full song with vocals and backing music. The model files are free to download and run on your own computer.
watch_out: Running it yourself needs a Linux computer with an NVIDIA graphics card with 24 GB of memory. Companies need a separate commercial license for the model files.

name: DiffRhythm 2
price_from: Free to run yourself (free online demo available)
good_for: An open model that writes full-length songs with vocals that follow your lyrics. The model files are free to download and run on your own computer.
watch_out: Running it yourself takes command-line steps and Python, so it suits technical users. You can try it free in your web browser on its Hugging Face demo page.

name: StemRoller
good_for: Type a song name and it splits the song into vocals, drums, bass and everything else, plus an instrumental. Handy for making karaoke tracks.
watch_out: Splitting a song takes several minutes. You download the app and it runs on your own computer.

name: Jammable
good_for: Make AI cover songs: pick a voice from a library of 100,000+ voices, add your track and it sings it in that voice. It also has a voice changer and text to speech.
watch_out: There is no free plan; the cheapest plan is Basic at $8.99 a month. Many voices imitate real singers and characters, so check you are allowed to share what you make.

name: Wispr Flow
good_for: Speak instead of typing: press a key, talk, and your words are typed into any app. Works on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android in 100+ languages.
watch_out: The free plan is capped at 2,000 words a week on a computer and 1,000 words a week on a phone. Pro removes the cap.

name: Kokoro
good_for: A small, fast open text-to-speech model that reads text aloud in a natural voice. Light enough to run on an ordinary computer.
watch_out: It is a model, not an app, so you need some Python skills or a tool built on top of it. Check the model page for which languages and voices it covers.

name: Piper
good_for: A fast text-to-speech engine that runs fully on your own computer, with many free downloadable voices. Good for reading text aloud without sending it to the cloud.
watch_out: You install it from the command line, so it suits technical users. The project says it is looking for new maintainers.

name: F5-TTS
company: SWivid with the X-LANCE, SII and PCL labs
good_for: An open text-to-speech model that can copy the sound of a voice from a short sample recording. Runs on your own computer.
watch_out: The code is MIT licensed but the voice model files are licensed for non-commercial use only. Only copy voices you have permission to use. Setup needs Python.

name: Dia2
good_for: An open model that turns a script with two speakers into natural-sounding spoken dialogue, and can start speaking before the whole text is in.
watch_out: It only supports English and up to 2 minutes of audio at a time. Voices change from one try to the next unless you give it a voice sample. Setup needs a command line, and the guide is written for computers with an NVIDIA graphics card.

name: Buzz
good_for: A free app that turns audio and video into text, and translates it, entirely on your own computer using OpenAI's Whisper. Nothing has to be uploaded.
watch_out: The latest Mac version needs an Apple silicon Mac (the last Intel Mac version is 1.4.5). The Windows installer is not signed, so you will see a warning when you install it.

name: Vibe
good_for: A free app that transcribes audio and video files into text on your own device, with subtitles export and speaker labels. Works on Mac, Windows and Linux.
watch_out: Transcription speed depends on your computer. Optional summaries use the Claude API or Ollama, which you set up separately.

name: Handy
good_for: A free dictation app: hold a shortcut key, speak, and your words are typed into whatever text box you are using. It works on your own computer without sending audio to the cloud.
watch_out: It does one thing: turns your speech into text in the box you are typing in.

name: Liner
good_for: An AI research helper that searches the web and academic papers, and writes answers with sources. Also has deep research reports and file uploads.
watch_out: The free plan shows ads in answers and gives 100 credits a day and 1 file upload a day. A deep research request costs 40 credits.

name: Undermind
price_from: Free (Pro $20/month for academic users, $75/month for industry users)
good_for: A search tool for scientific papers: you describe your research, it reads hundreds of papers and builds a report with citations you can trace back to the source.
watch_out: Pro costs $20 a month for academic users but $75 a month for industry users; paying yearly lowers the academic price to $16 a month. The free plan has standard usage limits; Pro raises them 10 times.

name: Pixelcut
good_for: Remove backgrounds, erase objects, upscale photos and generate new backgrounds with AI, in a simple editor.
watch_out: On the free plan background removal and upscaling are limited. Pro includes 600 AI credits a month, and the stronger AI models spend those credits.

name: Draw Things
price_from: Free (Draw Things+ $8.99/month for more cloud power)
good_for: A free image-making app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that creates pictures from text on your own device, offline. It can also train your own custom styles on the device.
watch_out: It is built for Apple devices. Cloud compute needs a free account, and higher cloud limits and custom style uploads need Draw Things+ at $8.99 a month.

name: SwarmUI
good_for: A web page you run on your own computer for making AI images and video with models like Stable Diffusion and Flux. Gives you a lot of control.
watch_out: It is aimed at people comfortable installing software and picking models. Each model you download has its own license.

name: Easy Diffusion
good_for: A one-click installer that sets up Stable Diffusion on your own computer, with a friendly page for making pictures from text or from another image.
watch_out: It needs at least 8 GB of memory and 25 GB of free disk space. It can use an NVIDIA, AMD or Apple graphics chip, or run more slowly without one. The license forbids sharing images that break laws or cause harm.

name: Krita AI Diffusion
company: Acly and contributors (online service: Cosmic Interstice UG)
price_from: Free to run yourself (online service: token packs from €10, one-time)
good_for: A free plugin for the Krita painting app that adds AI image generation, inpainting and outpainting inside your drawing. Runs on your own hardware.
watch_out: You need to install Krita first and then set up the plugin. Running it on your own computer needs a strong graphics card with at least 6 GB of graphics memory, or it gets very slow. The online service needs no graphics card, but you pay for tokens after the free ones run out.

name: Typecast
good_for: Type or paste a script and pick an AI voice to read it aloud, with video export. Voice generation and playback are free; you spend credits when you download.
watch_out: The free plan allows about 5 minutes of audio downloads in total and requires you to credit Typecast on what you download. Basic includes about 35 minutes of downloads each month.

name: Msty Studio
price_from: Free (Aurum $149/year, billed annually; lifetime license $349 one-time)
good_for: A desktop app for chatting with AI models, either ones that run on your own computer or online ones, with personas, saved knowledge and prompt tools in one workspace.
watch_out: The free plan marks some features as limited, including persona chats, crew conversations and knowledge stacks. Msty Studio Web and the advanced features need the paid Aurum plan.

name: Open WebUI
price_from: Free to run yourself (Enterprise plans are by quote)
good_for: A free chat app for AI that you install yourself and use in your web browser. It works with AI models on your own computer (through Ollama) or online ones, and adds document chat, web search, voice and image tools.
watch_out: You install it yourself with a typed command (pip) or Docker, then connect an AI model. Business licenses, for rebranding and dedicated support, are sold only to companies.

name: Brave Leo
good_for: An AI assistant built into the Brave browser. Ask it questions, or have it summarize the web page, document or PDF you are looking at.
watch_out: Leo only comes with the Brave browser. Leo Premium adds more models and higher rate limits than the free version.

name: Lumo
good_for: A private AI chat assistant from Proton, the email and privacy company. You can try it without an account, and a free account lets you keep your chat history.
watch_out: The free plan limits use of the Max model, messages and chat history, and image generations, and allows 1 project. Lumo Plus raises those limits.

name: Google Antigravity
price_from: Free (Individual plan $0/month; paid Google AI plans add higher limits)
good_for: A downloadable app where AI agents build software for you. You describe what you want, and you can run several agents at once on different projects.
watch_out: The free Individual plan has basic weekly rate limits, so heavy users will hit the cap. Higher limits come with the paid Google AI Pro and Ultra plans.

name: Morphic
good_for: A free AI search engine that gives a complete answer with its sources instead of a list of links. Use it on its website, or run your own copy, because the code is open source.
watch_out: Running your own copy takes technical setup with Docker plus at least one AI provider key (OpenAI, Anthropic or Google, for example), and paid keys have their own costs.

name: Audimee
good_for: Turn a vocal recording into a different singing voice, split a song into vocals and instruments, and make harmonies. It is aimed at music makers.
watch_out: The free plan gives 15 minutes of conversions, MP3 downloads only and personal use only, with no harmony maker, and you cannot save your conversions. Starter includes 1 hour of conversions a month.

name: Submagic
good_for: Upload a short video and it adds captions automatically, plus free extra clips and sound, and lets you cut the video by editing its text.
watch_out: The $19/month Starter plan includes 45 credits (about 15 videos) a month and videos up to 2 minutes long. Automatic removal of silences and bad takes needs Pro ($39/month).

name: Vidu
good_for: Make short AI videos from text, from a photo, or from reference pictures of a character or object.
watch_out: The free plan is limited, for example 10 saved references a month. Standard includes 800 credits a month, which the page says covers up to 200 videos.

name: Basic Pitch
good_for: Drop in a recording of one instrument, or sing into your microphone, and get a MIDI file back that you can edit in music software. It is a free tool from Spotify.
watch_out: The online tool takes a recording of a single instrument or your singing, and gives you a MIDI file to clean up, not finished sheet music. There is also a version for programmers that you install with pip.

name: Crush
price_from: Free app (optional Hyper model service: free 100 credits/month, or $20/month)
good_for: A free AI coding helper that runs in your terminal, the text window where you type commands. You choose which AI model powers it, and you can keep several work sessions for each project.
watch_out: It works only by typing in a terminal window, so it suits people comfortable with the command line. You need a model: the Hyper service from the same company (100 free credits a month), or your own key from a provider like Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini.

name: MusicGPT
good_for: Type a description and get a full song, or make sound effects and spoken audio.
watch_out: The free plan gives 500 credits a month, and each download costs 50 credits. Plus includes 5,000 credits a month, 100 songs a month and unlimited free downloads; remix, edit and spoken audio (text to speech) come with Pro ($21.99/month).

name: AutoGPT
price_from: Free to run yourself (cloud Pro $50/month, 7-day free trial)
good_for: Build a team of AI helpers for research, content and sales work by describing the job in plain English. They can run on a schedule. A free version you set up and run yourself is also available.
watch_out: The cloud Pro plan needs a card to start the 7-day trial, then costs $50/month, and scheduled runs spend from a credit wallet with a cap you set for each helper. The free version you run yourself needs Docker setup and your own AI model keys.

name: Stability Matrix
good_for: A free app that installs and manages popular AI image tools such as ComfyUI, Fooocus and Forge with one click, and lets you browse and download models from CivitAI and Hugging Face.
watch_out: It sets up other image tools rather than being one itself, and you download the image models separately. Paid supporter plans add cloud extras and early builds; the $5/month Supporter plan includes 1,000 credits.

name: Dyad
good_for: A free desktop app that turns a plain-English description into a working web app on your own computer, using the AI model you choose. No sign-up is needed to download it.
watch_out: You bring your own AI access, such as an API key (a paid access code from an AI company), a ChatGPT subscription or a free local model. The free plan's built-in agent mode is limited to 20 messages a day; the fuller Pro Agent mode with its own AI credits comes with Pro at $20/month.

name: Clipdrop
good_for: Free web tools to remove backgrounds, erase unwanted objects, upscale pictures 2x, relight photos and remove text.
watch_out: The free plan allows 20 uses per 24 hours on background removal, upscaling, cleanup and relight, and 50 on text remover. Text-to-image, extending photos (Uncrop) and background replacement need Pro at $15/month, which also adds high-resolution output and 16x upscaling.

name: Pixlr
good_for: Edit photos and make AI images in your web browser. The Plus plan removes ads, allows unlimited saves and includes 80 AI credits each month.
watch_out: Plus's 80 monthly credits cover about 80 fast AI images or about 16 higher-quality ones. Unlimited fast image generations (fair use applies) need the Ultra plan, which starts at $24.99/month.

name: DomoAI
good_for: Turn text or pictures into short AI videos and images. The Basic plan includes character-to-video, talking avatars, 4K video upscaling and watermark-free results.
watch_out: Basic includes 600 credits a month, which the page says is about 85 videos or 150 images. Unlimited "Relax" generations on supported models start with the Standard plan at $42/month.

name: Magnific
good_for: One subscription for AI image, video, music and voice generation with many leading models, pro editing tools, a shared canvas for workflows called Spaces, and a stock library with a commercial AI license.
watch_out: Monthly Premium includes 20,000 credits a month. Unlimited generations need Premium+ at $45/month ($33.75/month billed annually). Prices exclude VAT and local taxes.

name: Viggle
good_for: Swap any character into trending clips, or turn a phone video into motion for your own character, to make memes and short social videos. The free plan includes 5 videos a day.
watch_out: Free allows one video at a time and keeps your files for 7 days. Pro at $9.99/month adds 80 credits a month, no watermark and permanent storage; access to all models needs the Live plan at $19.99/month.

name: D-ID
good_for: Make talking videos from a photo or one of 100+ stock avatars by typing a script. Lite includes 10 minutes of video a month and fast processing.
watch_out: Lite videos carry a D-ID watermark, and the commercial use license starts on Pro at $29/month. A free 14-day trial gives 3 minutes of video.

name: ResearchRabbit
good_for: Find research papers related to ones you already like. The free plan has unlimited searches across 310+ million articles and unlimited collections you can share.
watch_out: Free allows up to 50 seed articles. Up to 300 seed articles, advanced search controls and multiple projects need ResearchRabbit+ at $12.50/month ($10/month on the annual plan).

name: Wan2.2
price_from: Free to run yourself (the hosted Wan site has paid plans from $10/month)
good_for: Open-source AI video models from the Wan team that make video from a text prompt or a picture, which you can run on your own computer.
watch_out: The README says its main commands need a GPU with at least 80GB of video memory, while the smaller 5B model can run on a GPU with at least 24GB (such as an RTX 4090). Setup is done from the command line.

name: LTX-2
price_from: Free to run yourself (hosted LTX Studio from $15/month)
good_for: Lightricks' downloadable AI video models (the newest is LTX-2.5) that make video with synchronized sound from text or pictures, and also work inside the free ComfyUI tool.
watch_out: Setup is done from the command line and the model download is roughly 66 GiB. You must accept the model terms on Hugging Face to download it. The model is free for companies with under $10M in revenue; bigger companies need a commercial license.

name: Local Deep Research
good_for: An open-source research assistant you run yourself: it searches the web and your own documents with the AI model you choose, then writes a report with citations.
watch_out: Setup means installing Docker (a free tool that runs apps in sealed boxes) and pasting a command from the README, which also starts a local AI model and a private search tool. Web searches still go out to the internet, and if you connect a cloud AI model instead of a local one, your questions go to that provider.

name: Stockimg AI
good_for: Generate logos, posters, illustrations, wallpapers and stock-style pictures from a text description. Starter also includes AI background removal and 4x upscaling.
watch_out: Starter includes 300 credits a month. Unlimited credits need the Ultra plan at $48/month.

name: Mage
good_for: Make AI images in your browser with unlimited generations on base models such as Stable Diffusion and Flux 2, plus add-on styles (LoRAs) and inpainting (redrawing part of a picture).
watch_out: Basic includes 500 Gems a month and 2x speed. Unlimited video generation and ControlNet (pose and layout control) need Pro at $30/month.

name: Magenta RealTime 2
good_for: A free music model you play like an instrument on your Mac: hold a note or chord and it generates a matching ensemble, or type a description to make a playable sound. It comes as standalone apps and a plugin for music software.
watch_out: Real-time playing needs an Apple Silicon Mac. The small model runs on any, including MacBook Air; the larger one needs an M3 Pro or M2 Max or better. Model files download on first launch (about 450MB small, 2.5GB base).

name: bolt.diy
good_for: An open-source AI coding workspace where you pick the AI model for each prompt, from 21+ providers, and build complete web apps in your browser.
watch_out: You add your own AI provider keys (paid access codes from AI companies) or a local model. The README offers ready-made desktop installers, or a developer setup with Node.js and pnpm or Docker. One part it relies on (WebContainers) has separate commercial terms for large business use.

name: SD.Next
good_for: A free, open-source web interface for AI image and video generation on your own computer. It supports many models, which you pick from a list and it downloads automatically.
watch_out: Windows users can use the all-in-one installer and launcher; on other systems you install it from the terminal with git and a launch script. The README lists support for Nvidia, AMD, Intel Arc, Apple M1/M2 and CPU-only setups, so check its install guide for your hardware.

name: WanGP
price_from: Free to run on your own computer
good_for: One free local app for AI video, image and music with models such as Wan 2.2, LTX-2, Qwen Image, Flux and ACE-Step, using a browser interface.
watch_out: Its site says some models run on as little as 6 GB of video memory; others need more. The license lets you use it free but not sell WanGP itself or offer it as a paid hosted service.

name: Klangio
good_for: Turn recordings into sheet music: upload audio or a YouTube link and get notes, tabs or MIDI. The free plan transcribes demos of up to 20 seconds.
watch_out: Pro allows 50 transcriptions a month of up to 15 minutes each, with PDF, MIDI, Guitar Pro and MusicXML downloads. The Ultimate plan ($29.99/month, or $12.50/month billed annually) adds the plugin for music software and every transcription mode.

name: Google Flow
price_from: Free (paid plans from $4.99/month via Google AI Plus)
good_for: Google's AI studio for making videos and images: text to video, frames to video and image generation with models such as Veo and Nano Banana, free to try with a Google account.
watch_out: You must be 18 or older. The free plan gives 50 credits a day. 1080p video upscaling and higher limits start with Google AI Plus at $4.99/month; prices vary by market.

name: Scenario
good_for: A workspace for making game, product and brand art with 65+ AI models. The free tier gives 50 credits a day with no credit card; Starter includes 1,500 credits a month and private generations.
watch_out: Training your own custom models, unlimited relaxed generations and the priority queue need Pro at $45/month.

name: Base44
good_for: Describe the app you want in plain language and Base44 builds it with a database, sign-in and a visual editor. The free plan allows up to 5 apps.
watch_out: Free includes 25 message credits a month. Starter at $20/month gives 100 message credits and lets you connect your own domain.

name: screenpipe
good_for: Keeps your screen, audio and meetings on your own computer so you can search what you saw or heard, and share chosen context with AI tools such as Claude.
watch_out: It records your screen and audio, so think about what is on screen. The free plan searches recent work only; searching your full history needs Basic at $25/month.
